stem:
Pallavi multiplies $\dfrac{3}{8}\times\dfrac{4}{5}$ and then $\dfrac{4}{5}\times\dfrac{3}{8}$. She asks whether the products differ.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: $\dfrac{3}{8}\times\dfrac{4}{5}=\dfrac{4}{5}\times\dfrac{3}{8}$, because the order of the factors does not change the product.
The answer is the phrase fraction factors, with no product compared.
Writing the products is what creates the order of the two factors.
The product equals $\dfrac{3}{8}$, because $3$ and $8$ are the first numerals printed.

teacher.key_rationale: Fraction multiplication is commutative, so swapping the factors leaves the product unchanged. Naming fraction factors alone substitutes a label. Saying the writing creates the order reverses the relation. Grabbing the first printed numerals is surface capture.
